podcast.body: Nick Oliveri was Josh Homme's friend and played bass on the 1987 Sons of Kyuss demo. He later left the band and then rejoined. "Josh is buddy Nick Olivary, drummer Brett Bjork and singer John Garcia, recorded a demo."

podcast.title: Joined Queens of the Stone Age
podcast.body: Oliveri agreed to join Josh Homme's new band, Queens of the Stone Age, a moment captured in a phone message at the end of the debut album's track "I Was a Teenage Hand Model." "If you go right to the end of that debut Queens album, you'll find a song called I Was a Teenage Hand Model. And if you scrub to the end of the song, you'll hear this phone message. It's a little hard to make out, but that's Nick agreeing to be in Josh's new band."

xref.title: Josh Homme as Sole Member (Early 2004)
xref.body: In early 2004, following the firing of Nick Oliveri and the departure of Mark Lanegan, Josh Homme became the only remaining member of Queens of the Stone Age. He continued the band, given his primary role in writing 90% of the music and serving as the lead singer. "So this meant that in early 2004, Queen of the Stone Age was down to just one member, Josh Hommie."

xref.title: Nick Oliveri's Firing (2004)
xref.body: Bassist Nick Oliveri was fired by Josh Homme in 2004, primarily due to his "loose cannon" behavior, disrespect for fans, and "crazy partying" during the "Songs for the Deaf" tour in Australia. Other factors included aggression towards Homme over his then-girlfriend Brody Dalle, and Homme's suspicion that Oliveri was physically abusing his girlfriend. "All of a very was fired for disrespecting the group's fans, not to mention the crazy partying."

xref.title: Nick Oliveri's Firing (Early 2004)
xref.body: Bassist Nick Oliveri was fired by Josh Homme in early 2004 due to a series of "incidents occurring over the last 18 months." These included being arrested in Brazil for public nudity (performing in only sneakers), getting the band banned from a hotel in Australia, and, most critically, throwing full Corona beer bottles at the audience during a gig, pitched like fastballs. "A number of incidents occurring over the last 18 months have led to the decision that the two can no longer maintain a working partnership in the band."

xref.title: Nick Oliveri Fired, SWAT Standoff (July 12, 2011) – Domestic Abuse Leading to Career Ejection
xref.body: Nick Oliveri was initially fired from Queens of the Stone Age after being physically abusive to his girlfriend. After a truce appeared to be arranged, a SWAT team descended on his house on July 12, 2011, following an assault on his girlfriend. He was arrested on charges including drugs and weapons, faced up to 15 years in prison, and received a plea deal for probation and community service. Despite this, he can be heard as a contributor on the band's 2013 album *…Like Clockwork*, though he is no longer a full member. "Even though he faced up to 15 years in jail, he got a plea deal for probation and community service."

xref.title: Nick Oliveri's Domestic Standoff (2011)
xref.body: Nick Oliveri, a founding member of Queens of the Stone Age known for his volatile nature, was involved in a domestic dispute at his Hollywood home in July 2011. Police were called due to sounds of a disturbance, leading to a full SWAT team being dispatched late in the afternoon. This escalated into a five-hour standoff that concluded at 10:30 PM when Oliveri surrendered. Upon searching the residence, law enforcement found a loaded rifle, and he was subsequently arrested on domestic violence charges. "Cops were called when they heard sounds of a disturbance. A full SWAT team was dispatched late in the afternoon, which was the start of a five-hour standoff that didn't end until 1030 that night."

xref.title: Lineup Instability and Label Issues
xref.body: The band experienced numerous lineup changes, including Nick Oliveri leaving and returning, and two different drummers and bass players over time. They also faced challenges when their record label went under and they were absorbed into Elektra, a major label part of the Warner Empire, which they disliked. "And the low light was probably all the lineup changes. Nick all of a very left and came back. The band went through two drummers and two bass players. And there were other problems. Their record label went under and they got absorbed into Elektra, part of the major label Warner Empire. That didn't sit well with them."

xref.title: Nick Oliveri's Legal Troubles
xref.body: Oliveri's history includes an arrest in 1999 for fighting with the British band Terrorvision, and his arrest at the 2001 Rock in Rio Festival for playing naked. On July 12, 2011, he was involved in a two-and-a-half-hour standoff with a SWAT team in LA, leading to his arrest and charges of felony domestic violence. He later received a plea bargain for cocaine possession, community service, and anger management. "On July 12, 2011, he was engaged in a standoff with a SWAT team in LA. After two and a half hours, he was arrested and charged with felony domestic violence."

xref.title: Reconciliation and Continued Collaboration
xref.body: Despite his past issues, Nick Oliveri eventually patched things up with Josh Homme, working together in the studio for background vocals on "Like Clockwork" and performing together on stage in 2014. Oliveri expressed a desire to rejoin Queens full-time, though this appears unlikely. "It took years, but things got patched up between him and Josh. They even worked in the studio together."

xref.body: Despite his departure, Josh Homme and Nick Oliveri have reconciled their differences, even though Oliveri has not significantly rejoined the band's activities. "Nicola Vary has never re-entered the picture much, but he and Josh have long since reconciled."
